newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand orders 16 finance firms to merge,consolidate.
newsitem.headline: Thailand orders 16 finance firms to merge,consolidate.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Friday that it had ordered 16 finance companies to stop operations and submit plans for mergers or consolidations with other parties to authorities in two weeks.

Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond told a news conference that the companies were suspended because of concerns that their poor financial positions could harm depositors' interests. The names of the finance firms suspended were:

Finance One Plc, General Finance and Securities Plc, CMIC FInance and Securities, Dynanic Eastern Finance Thailand Plc, Prime Finance and Securities Plc, ITF Finance and Securities Plc ITFn.BK and Thai Financial Trust Plc.

CL Sahaviriya Finance and Securities, United Finance Corp Plc, GCN Finance Plc, Sub Thamrong Finance Co Ltd, Thai Fuji Finance and Securities, Thana One Finance and Securities Co Ltd, Country Finance Co Ltd, Srinakorn Finance and Securities Co Ltd and Royal International Finance and Securities Co Ltd.
Rerngchai added that five strong finance companies would be leaders of the mergers and consolidations that weaker finance firms had been ordered to undertake.
The 16 suspended firms will have to merge with one or more of the five stronger companies.

A senior central bank official said the leaders of the mergers would be Dhana Siam Finance and Securities Plc, Nava Finance and Securities Plc, National Finance and Securities Plc, Phatra Thanakit Finance and Securities Plc and Krungthai Thanakit Plc.
The central bank planned to grant two to five new bank licences to major merged firms, Rerngchai said.
Those who could be eligible for the new bank licences would need to have total capital and assets of 150 billion baht ($6 billion).
"We will grant two to five new bank licenses, but we will have to look at granting them on a case by case basis," the governor said.

Those groups of finance firms that merged but failed to obtain new bank licences would be classified as super finance firms that would be allowed to undertake a wider range of financial businesses, he added.
"What we are doing is in line with international standards. I am confident that the meaasures that we launched and will be implemented are in the right direction," he said.
"I believe it will restore foreign investor confidence (in Thailand)."
Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya, who was also at the news conference, said depositors need not worry because they would be protected by the authorities if any of the companies went under.
